s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 enabled GST?
x: The Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 enabled GST; 122nd was the number of the Bill introduced in 2014.

s: When GST came into force on July 1, 2017, what did it subsume?
x: GST subsumed 17 taxes and 13 cesses when it came into force on July 1, 2017. The other combinations interchange or alter these two figures.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct regarding items outside GST?
o: Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is outside GST
Basic Customs Duty is outside GST
x: Natural gas is among the petroleum items kept outside GST until the GST Council recommends otherwise.

s: In which month was India's highest-ever monthly gross GST collection of ₹2.43 lakh crore recorded?
x: The record ₹2.43 lakh crore came in April 2026; July 2026's ₹2.11 lakh crore was the third-highest.

s: At which GST Council meeting were the Next-Generation GST reforms approved?
x: They were approved at the 56th GST Council meeting and took effect in September 2025.

s: Who chairs the GST Council?
x: The GST Council (Article 279A) is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, not the RBI Governor.

s: To what rate was GST on toys cut from 12%?
x: GST on toys was cut from 12% to 5%.

s: On which date did GST come into effect in India?
x: GST came into effect on 1 July 2017, through the 101st Amendment Act, 2016.

s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the GST Council?
x: Article 279A provides for the GST Council; 246A gives GST law-making power and 269A covers inter-State supplies.

s: What kind of consumption tax is GST?
x: GST is a destination-based consumption tax, not origin-based.

s: Which of the following GST milestone–year pairs is correctly matched?
o: Union Budget proposes a national GST – 2003
x: The 122nd Amendment Bill came in 2014; the Kelkar Task Force was 2003, the Budget proposal 2006 and the 101st Amendment Act 2016.

s: How did July 2026's gross GST collection of ₹2.11 lakh crore rank?
x: July 2026 was the third-highest; the highest is April 2026 at ₹2.43 lakh crore.

s: What were the gross GST collections for 2025–26?
x: Gross GST rose from ₹7.4 lakh crore (2017–18) to ₹22.27 lakh crore (2025–26).

s: Under the Next-Generation GST reforms, the registration threshold for goods was raised from ₹20 lakh to how much?
x: The goods threshold rose from ₹20 lakh to ₹40 lakh.

s: Which Article–GST provision pair is correctly matched?
x: Article 269A covers inter-State GST; 246A gives concurrent law-making power and 279A provides the GST Council.

s: Which body recommended GST in 2003?
o: Kelkar Task Force on Indirect Taxes
x: The Kelkar Task Force on Indirect Taxes (2003) recommended GST.

s: Which body implements GST at the Centre?
x: GST is implemented by the CBIC (HQ New Delhi, Ministry of Finance).

s: Under the Next-Generation GST reforms of September 2025, what rate applies to luxury and sin goods?
x: The main slabs are 5% and 18%, with 40% for luxury and sin goods.

s: At what level did the RBI keep the repo rate unchanged in August 2026, while revising its 2026–27 CPI forecast to 5.0%?
x: The repo rate stayed at 5.25% while the CPI forecast was trimmed from 5.1% to 5.0%; 5.00% is the SDF and 5.50% the MSF/Bank Rate.

s: The RBI revised its 2026–27 core inflation forecast from 4.7% to what?
x: The RBI revised the core inflation forecast from 4.7% to 4.3%.

s: Under Flexible Inflation Targeting, who sets the inflation target every five years?
x: The target is set by the Government of India every five years; the RBI Act was amended in May 2016 to introduce FIT.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee?
o: It is chaired by a Deputy Governor
Its external members serve for 4 years
x: The MPC is chaired by the RBI Governor, not a Deputy Governor.

s: Which rate is now the floor of the RBI's liquidity adjustment corridor?
x: The SDF (5.00%) has replaced the reverse repo as the floor; MSF = Bank Rate = 5.50% is the ceiling.

s: As of August 2026, at what level did the Cash Reserve Ratio stand?
x: The CRR is 3% of NDTL after a 100 bps cut.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's August 2026 monetary policy:
1. The repo rate was held for the fourth consecutive time.
2. The decision was unanimous.
3. The policy stance was changed to accommodative.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: August was the 4th straight hold and was unanimous; the stance has stayed neutral since June 2025.

s: In August 2026, to what did the MPC revise its 2026–27 real GDP growth forecast?
x: The MPC raised its 2026–27 GDP forecast from 6.6% (June) to 6.7% (August).

s: The Monetary Policy Committee is constituted under which Section of the RBI Act?
x: The MPC is under Section 45ZB; Section 53 governs the RBI's surplus transfer.

s: In June 2026, at what level did the RBI keep the repo rate unchanged for the third consecutive pause?
x: The repo rate was held at 5.25% for the third consecutive pause.

s: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India nationalised?
x: The RBI was set up in 1935 and nationalised in 1949.

s: For how long do the external members of the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee serve?
x: External MPC members serve 4 years; quorum is 4 and the MPC meets at least 4 times a year.

s: What real GDP growth did the RBI Survey of Professional Forecasters (101st round) project for India for 2026–27?
x: The projection for 2026–27 was revised from 6.5% to 6.6%; 7% relates to 2027–28.

s: Under the RBI’s special FCNR(B) deposit swap facility, fresh deposits of what maturity may banks mobilise until September 2026?
x: Banks may mobilise fresh 3–5 year FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI measure, with eligibility until 30 September 2026. The tempting option of 1–3 years is incorrect because the specified maturity is 3–5 years.

s: At which rate is the RBI's special FCNR(B) deposit swap facility conducted?
x: The swap is at the FBIL Reference Rate, at par, once a week, in multiples of $1 million.

s: Who are eligible to hold the NRI deposit accounts covered by the RBI measure?
x: The eligible categories are NRIs, OCIs and PIOs. The other options omit one or more of these eligible categories.

s: The RBI's 101st Survey of Professional Forecasters described India's economy, growing neither overheating nor slowing, as a ____ economy.
x: The survey characterised the economy as Goldilocks, meaning growth is neither overheating nor slowing.

s: For what purpose is the NRO account of non-resident Indians used?
o: Hold fixed deposits in foreign currency
Swap foreign currency with the RBI
x: NRO manages income earned in India; NRE parks foreign earnings and FCNR(B) is a foreign-currency account.

s: According to the RBI Annual Report 2025–26, the Contingency Fund is intended to address which of the following?
x: The RBI Contingency Fund is meant for financial and monetary risks. Infrastructure and logistics risks are not identified as its purpose in the report.

s: With which function is Financial Benchmarks India Ltd (FBIL) associated?
x: FBIL provides benchmark and forex reference rates.

s: What growth did the IMF project for India for 2027–28?
x: The IMF put 2027–28 at 6.7%; its 2026–27 figure is 6.4%, and 6.6% is ADB's 2026–27 projection.

s: What is the base year of India's new Services Production Index?
x: The Services Production Index uses 2024–25 as its base year; its first experimental estimates came on 14 July 2026.

s: Who is the Chairman of the State Bank of India (established 1955, headquartered in Mumbai)?
x: C.S. Setty is the Chairman of SBI, which was established in 1955 and is headquartered in Mumbai.

s: What is the base year of the revised Wholesale Price Index (WPI)?
x: The WPI base was moved forward from 2011–12 to 2022–23, and items rose from 697 to 957.

s: Which State ranked first in per capita income for 2025–26 according to the RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian Economy?
x: Karnataka ranked first, with per capita income of ₹4,33,326 in 2025–26. Telangana ranked second at ₹4,18,931, while Andhra Pradesh recorded ₹2,94,507; hence neither is the correct answer.

s: How was the near-10% WPI inflation in June characterised?
o: Monetary inflation from excess money supply
x: It was cost-push/supply-shock inflation driven by fuel and power, manufactured products and food supply shocks, not demand-driven.

s: What is the base year of the revised Consumer Price Index (CPI), used by the MPC?
x: The revised CPI has 2024 as its base year and is used by the MPC.

s: What unemployment rate, the lowest in eight years, did PLFS 2025 record for India?
x: PLFS 2025 recorded unemployment at 3.1%, the lowest in eight years.

s: Which of the following was identified as a factor behind the rise in India's external debt?
x: US dollar valuation effects contributed to the rise in external debt; the other options would reduce debt.

s: What was India's GDP growth in FY 2025–26 according to the official data?
x: India's GDP growth in FY 2025–26 was 7.7%. The 7.1% figure relates to FY 2024–25, while 7.9% was the GVA growth rate.

s: How is GDP calculated?
o: GVA plus subsidies minus taxes plus depreciation
x: GDP equals GVA plus (product) taxes minus subsidies.

s: In which year did the FRBM Act come into effect?
x: The FRBM Act came into effect in 2003; 2019 is the year the NSO was formed.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's price indices?
o: The WPI is compiled by the National Statistics Office
Food has a higher weight in the CPI than in the WPI
x: The WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser in DPIIT, not by the NSO.

s: Which new index has replaced the WPI as the deflator for the IIP?
x: The new Output PPI (base 2022–23) is now the IIP deflator instead of WPI.

s: After its first experimental estimates, how often will the Services Production Index be released?
x: It will be released monthly on the 29th with a lag of about 60 days.

s: What was India's WPI inflation in July 2026?
x: WPI inflation was 9.78% in July 2026 after nearly 10% in June, a cost-push rise.

s: What growth did ADB project for India for 2027–28?
x: ADB projects 7.3% for 2027–28 and 6.6% for 2026–27.

s: India's external debt at end-March 2026 was about what share of GDP?
x: External debt was USD 762.8 bn, or 20.8% of GDP, up from 19.8%.

s: Which fiscal deficit target did the Centre meet in 2025–26?
x: The 4.4% target was met with an actual deficit of ₹15.19 lakh crore.

s: In which year was the National Statistics Office (NSO) formed?
x: The NSO was formed in 2019.

s: What was India's projected public capital expenditure for FY27?
x: Public capex was projected at ₹12.2 lakh crore for FY27, up from ₹2 lakh crore in FY15.

s: Which of the following States is NOT among the rare earth corridors announced in the Union Budget 2026–27?
x: The rare earth corridors are in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

s: For which States does the Union Budget 2026–27 provide 4,000 electric buses?
x: 4,000 e-buses are planned for the Purvodaya States.

s: Who is the Chief Economic Adviser associated with the Economic Survey 2026?
x: V. Anantha Nageswaran is the Chief Economic Adviser.

s: According to the Economic Survey 2026, India's maize yield rose from 2.56 t/ha in FY16 to how much?
x: Maize yield rose to 3.78 t/ha in FY25.

s: The Coconut Promotion Scheme in the Union Budget 2026–27 is part of a ₹350 crore allocation for what?
x: It is part of ₹350 crore for high-value agriculture: coconut, cashew and cocoa.

s: What is the outlay of Biopharma SHAKTI announced in the Union Budget 2026–27?
x: Biopharma SHAKTI gets ₹10,000 crore for biologics and biosimilars.

s: The MoU for introducing UPI in Seychelles was signed between NIPL and which institution?
x: The MoU was signed between NIPL and the Central Bank of Seychelles, with UPI planned by the end of 2026. ACLEDA Bank is associated with the Cambodia arrangement, not this MoU.

s: On which date did the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), developed by NPCI, complete ten years?
x: UPI, developed by NPCI, completed ten years on 25 August 2026.

s: In 2024, UPI accounted for approximately what share of global real-time payment volume?
x: UPI accounted for about 49% of global real-time payment volume in 2024; the IMF called it the largest such system by volume.

s: Which UPI milestone–year pair is correctly matched?
x: BHIM came in December 2016; the pilot was April–August 2016, Dynamic QR 2017 and UPI 2.0 2018.

s: Which combination of UPI developments belongs to the 2020–22 period?
o: Credit Line on UPI, UPI 2.0 and mandates
Dynamic QR, BHIM app and IPO payments
AutoPay, UPI 123PAY, UPI Lite and credit cards
Pilot with 21 banks, public rollout and BHIM app
x: The 2020–22 period saw AutoPay, UPI 123PAY for feature phones, UPI Lite and credit-card integration. The milestone of five billion monthly transactions was reached in March 2022.

s: What is the defining feature of UPI Circle?
o: A secondary user can make payments from the primary user's account
A bank can link overdrafts through UPI 2.0
A feature-phone user can make payments through UPI 123PAY
A user can pay IPO application money through SEBI
x: UPI Circle allows a secondary user to pay from the primary user's account. Biometric authentication on the device and Aadhaar face authentication are also associated with this feature.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UPI milestones?
o: UPI crossed 1 billion monthly transactions in October 2019
The BHIM app was launched in December 2016
Credit Line on UPI was introduced in 2019
x: Credit Line on UPI came in 2023, not 2019.

s: The Nifty500 Ahimsa Index, launched in July 2026, includes only companies in which category?
x: Only Green-category companies are included, not Orange ones.

s: Through a partnership between NIPL and which bank was UPI launched in Greece?
x: UPI in Greece was launched through the NIPL–Eurobank partnership; NIPL was set up in 2020.

s: In which country was UPI's first international deployment?
x: Bhutan, not Nepal, was UPI's first international deployment; UPI was developed by NPCI.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about UPI in the Maldives?
o: The Maldives is listed as the 12th country to adopt UPI
UPI was launched there on 30 July 2026
UPI was linked with the Favara system
Favara belongs to the Maldives Monetary Authority
x: UPI is live in 11 countries, so the Maldives is not the 12th.

s: Which organisation, headquartered in Mumbai, operates products such as UPI, RuPay, IMPS, Bharat BillPay and FASTag?
o: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
x: The National Payments Corporation of India, established in 2008 and headquartered in Mumbai, operates these payment products. NPCI International Payments Limited is its subsidiary for international expansion rather than the organisation described in the question.

s: Which RBI Governor inaugurated the UPI pilot, launched on 11 April 2016 in Mumbai with 21 banks?
x: Raghuram Rajan inaugurated the pilot; UPI went live for the public on 25 August 2016.

s: UPI is built on which payment system?
x: UPI, developed by NPCI and regulated by the RBI, is built on IMPS.

s: By August 2026, UPI was live in how many countries?
x: The list rose from 8 countries in March 2026 to 11 by August 2026.

s: Which country issued the world's first polymer currency notes, in 1988?
x: Australia issued the first polymer notes in 1988; Canada, the UK and Singapore followed.

s:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's experimental polymer notes:
1. 100 crore units each of ₹10 and ₹20 notes are planned.
2. Polymer notes last 2.5–6 times longer than paper notes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: 100 crore units each of ₹10 and ₹20, lasting 2.5–6 times longer.

s: On which date did UPI go live for the public?
x: The UPI pilot began on 11 April 2016; it went live for the public on 25 August 2016.

s: Which organisation developed e-RUPI, the purpose-specific digital e-voucher launched in August 2021?
x: e-RUPI was developed by NPCI on the UPI platform with DFS, MoHFW and the National Health Authority.

s: In which year was e-RUPI, a cashless QR code or SMS-based e-voucher, launched?
x: PM Narendra Modi launched e-RUPI on 2 August 2021.

s: What is the wallet limit of UPI Lite?
x: UPI Lite wallet: ₹5,000 (₹1,000 per transaction); UPI 123PAY: ₹10,000.

s: PM Dhan Dhanya Krishi Yojana, approved in July 2025, covers how many low-performing districts?
x: The scheme covers 100 low-performing districts, not 110.

s: What was India's insurance penetration in FY25?
x: Penetration was 2.7% of GDP in FY25; 3.2% was the pandemic peak.

s: According to RBI and IRDAI data, life insurers hold about what share of outstanding Central Government dated securities?
x: Life insurers hold nearly one-fourth of outstanding Central Government dated securities.

s: Which is the single largest institutional holder of Government of India debt, designated a Domestic Systemically Important Insurer?
x: LIC is the single largest institutional holder of GoI debt and a designated D-SII.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Establishment of SBI and the National Agricultural Credit (Long-term Operations) Fund
2. Nationalisation of 14 banks
3. Establishment of NABARD
4. SHG-Bank Linkage Programme
Which scheme–launch year pair is correctly matched?
x: KCC began in 1998; PMJDY was 2014, MUDRA 2015 and the Jan Samarth Portal and e-KCC 2022.

s: What was the Ground Level Credit target for FY 2025–26?
x: The Ground Level Credit target for FY 2025–26 was ₹32.50 lakh crore, including ₹5 lakh crore for animal husbandry, dairy and fisheries.

s: NRLM was launched in 2010 by restructuring which scheme?
x: NRLM was launched in 2010 after restructuring SGSY and renamed DAY-NRLM on 29 March 2016.

s: Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, what is the effective interest rate for farmers?
x: Loans at 7% with 3% prompt-repayment incentive bring the farmer's effective rate to 4%.

s: How many Regional Rural Banks make up India's RRB network (22,000+ branches in 700 districts)?
x: The RRB network has 28 RRBs with more than 22,000 branches covering 700 districts.

s: Which of the following about farmer welfare schemes is NOT correct?
o: PM-KISAN gives ₹6,000 a year and covers 9.44 crore families
PMFBY insures more than 4 crore farmers every year
PM-KMY gives a pension of ₹2,000 a month after age 60
Women are more than 25% of PM-KISAN beneficiaries
x: PM-KMY pension is ₹3,000 per month after age 60, not ₹2,000.

s: Up to how much may a Navratna company invest without prior Government approval?
x: A Navratna may invest up to ₹1,000 crore or 15% of its net worth without Government approval.

s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Establishment of CPCL at Chennai
2. Establishment of GRSE at Kolkata
3. Introduction of the Navratna scheme
x: GRSE was set up in 1884 at Kolkata, CPCL in 1965 at Chennai, and the Navratna scheme dates from 1997.

s: What is the EPF interest rate for 2025–26, fixed by the CBT?
x: The CBT kept EPF at 8.25% for the third straight year; the Finance Ministry concurred in June 2026.

s:
Consider the following statements about small savings rates for July–September 2026:
1. The Public Provident Fund carries 7.1%.
2. The National Savings Certificate carries 8.2%.
3. The Senior Citizens Savings Scheme carries 8.2%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Small savings rates were unchanged: PPF 7.1%, NSC 7.7%, Sukanya Samriddhi and SCSS 8.2%.

s: Which insurance initiative–feature pair is correctly matched?
x: Bima Vahak is women-led distribution; Bima Sugam is the digital marketplace and Bima Vistaar the affordable product.

s: In which year was NABARD, which marked its 45th Foundation Day on 12 July 2026, established?
x: NABARD was established in 1982.

s: Since which year has the Navratna scheme for central public sector enterprises been in place?
x: The Navratna scheme began in 1997; a Navratna may invest up to ₹1,000 crore or 15% of net worth without approval.

s: In which year were 14 banks nationalised?
x: 14 banks were nationalised in 1969, more in 1980.

s: On which date was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana launched?
x: PMJDY was launched on 28 August 2014.

s: Who chairs the Central Board of Trustees (CBT) of the EPFO, which fixed the 8.25% EPF rate for 2025-26?
x: The CBT, chaired by Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, fixed 8.25% on 2 March 2026.

s: Which defence PSU, established in 1884 at Kolkata, got Navratna status in 2026?
x: Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers (GRSE), est. 1884, Kolkata, is a Navratna.

s: Where is the Asian Development Bank, which funds the North-East bamboo project, headquartered?
x: ADB is headquartered in Manila; its bamboo loan is USD 42.2 million for 6 North-Eastern States.

s: How much is the ADB loan for Chennai's water and sanitation project?
x: The ADB loan of USD 230 million is for water and sanitation in Chennai.

s: Under the Aviation Turbine Fuel Price Stabilisation Fund, compensation is provided when the ____ exceeds the notified benchmark.
x: Compensation is triggered when the import-parity price exceeds the benchmark; support to OMCs is interest-free.

s: Operational airports in India rose from 74 in 2014 to how many by July 2026?
x: Operational airports rose from 74 to 165; India is the third-largest domestic aviation market.

s: What is the outlay of the Samudra Manthan National Offshore Exploration Scheme, approved on 31 July 2026?
x: The scheme was approved on 31 July 2026 with an outlay of ₹84,084 crore.

s: Under UDAN, what was the approximate fare cap for a flight of about one hour or 500 km?
x: UDAN capped fares at about ₹2,500 for a one-hour or roughly 500-km flight.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the PM Surya Sarovar Yojana?
o: It was approved on 31 July 2026 for 5,000 MW of floating solar with co-located storage
Reservoirs and industrial ponds are eligible sites
It requires a minimum storage of 3 hours
All States and UTs are eligible
x: The minimum storage requirement is 2 hours (10,000 MWh), not 3 hours.

s: From where did PM Narendra Modi launch Modified UDAN on 4 July 2026?
x: PM Modi launched Modified UDAN from Jodhpur, Rajasthan; the original UDAN dates to October 2016.

s: What is the outlay of Modified UDAN for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36?
x: Modified UDAN has an outlay of ₹28,840 crore for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36.

s: Under Modified UDAN, how much has been allocated for developing 100 airports?
x: ₹12,159 crore is allocated for 100 airports, while about ₹10,043 crore is for VGF.

s: The first UDAN flight, in April 2017, operated on which route?
x: The first UDAN flight operated on the Shimla–Delhi route in April 2017.

s: The BHAVYA scheme aims to develop how many investment-ready industrial parks in six years?
x: BHAVYA targets 100 investment-ready industrial parks over six years with an outlay of ₹33,660 crore.

s: Which body developed the BHAVYA portal, launched by Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal?
x: The portal was developed by NICDC, not DPIIT.

s: The Mission for Cotton Productivity targets raising lint productivity from 441 kg/ha to ____ by 2031.
x: The mission targets 755 kg/ha lint productivity by 2031, up from 441 kg/ha in TE 2025–26.

s: Under the BHAVYA industrial parks scheme, what is the NICDC–State participation ratio?
x: NICDC–State participation is 51:49; States give land and the Centre gives infrastructure.

s: Which organisation released the BHAVYA guidelines in May 2026?
x: The BHAVYA guidelines were released by DPIIT in May 2026. NICDC developed the portal, while BIS and FSSAI are among the testing partners associated with the industrial parks.

s: Under BHAVYA, what park size applies to mid-sized States?
x: Mid-sized States get parks of 100–500 acres; up to 1,000 acres applies near cities and 25 acres in hilly/NE areas.

s: In which group of States were the Mega Leather, Footwear and Accessories Clusters approved?
o: Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu
Bihar, Assam, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu
Madhya Pradesh, Nagaland, Tripura and Tamil Nadu
x: The clusters were approved in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, with an outlay of ₹898 crore. The other options replace one or more of these States with States associated with the bamboo industry project.

s: In which year was the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) established?
x: PNGRB was set up in 2006 under the PNGRB Act, 2006.

s: With which Ministry are the Mega Leather, Footwear and Accessories Clusters associated?
x: The clusters are associated with the Ministry of Commerce and Industry; the main export markets are the USA, EU and UK.

s: Under the Incentive Scheme for Promotion of Domestic PNG Connections, the incentive is given to:
x: CGD entities get 200 SCM of low-cost APM gas per billed domestic connection above the threshold, in two instalments over six months.

s: Which Oil Marketing Companies are covered under the Aviation Turbine Fuel Price Stabilisation Fund?
o: Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and ONGC
Bharat Petroleum, Hindustan Petroleum and Oil India
Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and GAIL
Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum
x: The three OMCs are Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum.

s: What is the outlay of the BHAVYA scheme for 100 industrial parks?
x: BHAVYA's outlay is ₹33,660 crore; ₹28,840 crore is Modified UDAN and ₹84,084 crore Samudra Manthan.

s: Who is the President of the Asian Development Bank?
x: Masato Kanda heads the ADB (est. 1966, Manila); Ajay Banga heads the World Bank.

s: The Mission for Cotton Productivity, with an outlay of ₹5,659 crore, covers which period?
x: The Union Cabinet approved ₹5,659 crore for 2026–27 to 2030–31.

s: The target of the Solar Parks Scheme was raised from 20 GW to how much?
x: The target was raised to 40 GW; 54 parks with 39,188 MW were sanctioned by February 2026.

s: On which date was the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana launched?
x: It was launched on 13 February 2024 with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore for one crore households.

s: In which year was the Solar Parks Scheme introduced?
x: The Solar Parks Scheme came in 2014; the National Solar Mission was launched in 2010.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about solar irrigation?
o: Groundwater irrigation emits 45–62 billion tonnes of CO₂ a year
Suryashakti Kisan Yojana is a scheme of Gujarat
In Bangladesh's fee-for-service model, solar irrigation was 20–30% cheaper than diesel
x: Groundwater irrigation emits 45–62 million tonnes of CO₂ a year, not billion tonnes.

s: In July 2026, what was India's approximate installed wind power capacity?
x: Wind capacity was 58.14 GW; 164.59 GW is the solar capacity.

s: Under Panchamrit, what is India's net-zero target year?
x: Panchamrit sets net-zero by 2070, along with 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030.

s: By 30 June 2026, what had India's total solar capacity reached?
x: Solar capacity grew from about 3 GW in 2014 to 162.15 GW, including 118.79 GW from large projects.

s: What is the primary purpose of the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM), introduced in 2019?
o: To provide free electricity to one crore households
To provide a quality framework for PV modules and cells
To finance standalone solar pumps on farms
To establish solar parks with a target of 40 GW
x: ALMM, introduced in 2019, is a quality framework for PV modules and cells. Free household electricity, standalone solar pumps and solar-park development are associated with other programmes or schemes.

s: To what does Component B of PM-KUSUM relate?
x: Component B covers standalone solar pumps; A is plants on barren land and C is solarising grid pumps.

s: In which year did India propose One Sun One World One Grid (OSOWOG)?
x: India proposed OSOWOG in 2018; GGI–OSOWOG was launched with the UK at COP26 in 2021.

s: Which scheme installed more than 2.5 million solar pumps in five years and has a 2.0 version being prepared?
x: PM-KUSUM installed more than 2.5 million solar pumps in five years, and PM-KUSUM 2.0 is being prepared.

s: Which State runs the water-saving scheme 'Pani Bachao, Paisa Kamao'?
x: Pani Bachao, Paisa Kamao is Punjab's; Haryana runs Mera Pani Meri Virasat and Gujarat Suryashakti Kisan Yojana.

s: Which solar park/transmission pair is correctly matched?
x: Rewa is in Madhya Pradesh; Bhadla is 2,245 MW, Pavagada is in Karnataka, and the Green Energy Corridor evacuated 24,567.8 MW.

s: Which two countries co-founded the International Solar Alliance at COP21 in Paris in 2015?
x: The International Solar Alliance was co-founded by India and France at COP21 in Paris in 2015. The other country combinations do not represent the founding partnership specified for the Alliance.

s: On which date is Global Wind Day observed every year?
x: Global Wind Day is observed on 15 June; the 2026 conference theme was "Wind Energy: From Ambition to Acceleration".

s: India is recognised as which of the following in the global coal sector?
o: The 2nd-largest coal producer but 4th-largest coal consumer
x: India is the 2nd-largest coal producer and the 2nd-largest coal consumer. The other options alter one or both of these rankings; the 3rd and 4th positions mentioned in the energy context relate to renewable capacity, wind and crude refining, not to both coal measures.

s: How many solar parks with what capacity does Andhra Pradesh have under the Solar Parks Scheme?
x: By February 2026, AP had 5 solar parks of 4,200 MW.

s: Under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, up to how many units of free electricity a month are given?
x: PM Surya Ghar gives up to 300 units free to 1 crore households; outlay ₹75,021 crore.

s: On which date did the 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam achieve first criticality?
x: The PFBR achieved first criticality on 6 April 2026, not 2025.

s: The Ethanol Blending Roadmap 2020–25 advanced the E20 target year from 2030 to which year?
x: The Roadmap advanced the E20 target from 2030 to 2025, and India achieved it.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ethanol blends?
o: E85 contains 51–83% ethanol and requires a flex-fuel vehicle
Ethanol has a RON of about 108
E100 is a blend containing 20% ethanol
x: E100 is not a 20% ethanol blend; it is E20 that contains 20% ethanol.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about biofuel feedstocks?
o: Groundnut and horse gram are identified biofuel feedstocks
First-generation ethanol feedstocks include sugarcane, molasses, maize and rice
Second-generation feedstocks include rice/wheat straw, bagasse and bamboo
Cassava, damaged wheat, rotten potatoes and sugar beet are identified feedstocks
x: Groundnut and horse gram are not among the identified biofuel feedstocks; the 1G, 2G and additional feedstocks listed are correct.

s: Where is the green ammonia bunkering hub at V.O. Chidambaranar Port located?
x: V.O. Chidambaranar Port is at Thoothukudi; Phase 1 of the hub is planned for 200 KTPA by 2029–30.

s: The Atomic Energy Act 1962 replaced the Atomic Energy Act of which year?
x: The Atomic Energy Act 1962 replaced the 1948 Act.

s: Through which process is biogas, mainly methane and carbon dioxide, produced?
x: Biogas is produced by anaerobic digestion, not aerobic digestion.

s: The SATAT initiative, launched in 2018, targeted how many compressed biogas (CBG) plants by 2023?
x: SATAT targeted 5,000 CBG plants by 2023, but only 132 were completed by 3 June 2026.

s: Under the National Green Hydrogen Mission, what is the full form of SIGHT?
o: Scheme for Indigenous Green Hydrogen Technology
Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition
Support for Innovation in Green Hydrogen Technologies
Strategic Initiative for Green Hydrogen Trade
x: SIGHT is Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition; the mission's nodal ministry is MNRE.

s: What annual green hydrogen production does the National Green Hydrogen Mission target by 2030?
x: The 2030 target is 5 MMT of green hydrogen per year, with ₹1 lakh crore import savings and 50 MMT CO2 avoided.

s:
Assertion (A): The Nuclear Energy Mission targets 100 GW by 2031-32.
Reason (R): The Nuclear Energy Mission targets 100 GW by 2047.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true. The mission targets 100 GW by 2047, while its capacity target for 2031-32 is 22.38 GW, not 100 GW.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Samudra Manthan Scheme – Central Sector Scheme of MoPNG up to 2030–31
Operator's insurance or financial security – Retained until spent fuel leaves the pool
Department of Atomic Energy – Established in 1954, Mumbai, under the Prime Minister
In-principle approval – Granted only after site and technology clearance
x: In-principle approval is possible before site or technology clearance, not only after it.

s: What is the outlay of the National Green Hydrogen Mission, launched in January 2023?
x: The Mission has an outlay of ₹19,744 crore and targets 5 MMT of green hydrogen by 2030.

s: India's first indigenous hydrogen train was reported in July 2026 on which section?
x: India's first indigenous hydrogen train was reported on the Jind–Sonipat section.

s: Which feedstocks are associated with E20 petrol production?
x: E20 ethanol feedstocks include maize, damaged grain and biomass.

s: Where is the NTPC green hydrogen hub located in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The NTPC green hydrogen hub in Andhra Pradesh is located at Pudimadaka. Paradip, Deendayal and V.O. Chidambaranar are listed as Green Hydrogen Hub ports, not the Andhra Pradesh location of the NTPC hub.

s: Which company is associated with the green ammonia bunkering hub at V.O. Chidambaranar Port, Thoothukudi?
x: AM Green is associated with the green ammonia bunkering hub at V.O. Chidambaranar Port.

s: Under the CBG Blending Obligation approved by the National Biofuels Coordination Committee, what is the prescribed blending level for FY26?
x: The CBG blending obligation begins at 1% in FY26 and rises to 5% by FY29. The 5% figure is the FY29 level, not the starting level for FY26.

s: What is the Centre's present position on increasing ethanol blending in petrol beyond E20?
o: There is no proposal at present to raise blending beyond 20%.
x: The Centre has stated that there is no proposal at present to increase blending beyond 20%; any future move depends on scientific studies and consultations. The other options incorrectly suggest an immediate increase or a reduction below E20.

s: Which of the following about types of hydrogen is NOT correct?
o: Grey – steam methane reforming of natural gas
x: Blue hydrogen comes from steam methane reforming of natural gas with carbon capture; coal gasification gives brown hydrogen.

s: Where is the 2G bamboo ethanol plant cited in the ethanol sustainability debate located?
x: The 2G bamboo ethanol plant is at Golaghat, Assam.

s: Which ports have been named hydrogen hub ports?
x: Deendayal, V.O. Chidambaranar and Paradip are the hydrogen hub ports.

s: The 5F Vision of PM MITRA parks is Farm → Fibre → Factory → Fashion → ____.
x: The 5F Vision runs Farm → Fibre → Factory → Fashion → Foreign.

s: China is the leading refiner in how many of the 20 strategic minerals?
x: China leads refining in 19 of 20 strategic minerals and holds over 90% of rare-earth refining.

s: How many PM MITRA mega textile parks have been provided for under the scheme (2021-22 to 2027-28)?
x: Seven PM MITRA parks have been provided for with an outlay of ₹4,445 crore for 2021-22 to 2027-28.

s: What was India's approximate mobile phone production in 2025–26?
x: Mobile phone production was about ₹6.27 lakh crore; ₹2.59 lakh crore was mobile exports and ₹4.24 lakh crore electronics exports.

s: Where did Singareni Collieries Company Limited begin its first gold and copper exploration in Karnataka on 27 August 2026?
x: SCCL began exploration at Lingadahalli in Devadurga Taluk of Raichur district; the agreement was signed in Bengaluru.

s: When was the India–US framework on critical minerals and rare earths signed?
x: The India–US critical minerals and rare earths framework was signed in May 2026.

s: India holds which rank in global limestone production?
x: India ranks 2nd in limestone production. The other ranks listed correspond to India's positions in zinc, iron ore and bauxite, not limestone.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's toy trade?
o: Toy exports grew by 151.9% between 2017–18 and 2025–26
Toy exports were US$152.7 million in 2017–18
Toy exports reached US$384.7 million in 2025–26
India's toy trade surplus in 2025–26 was US$213.01 million
x: The 2025–26 surplus was US$152 million; US$213.01 million was the 2017–18 deficit.

s: How many critical minerals has India identified?
x: India has identified 30 critical minerals; the MMDR Act, 1957, amended in 2023, lets the Centre auction them.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Quality Control Order for Toys, 2020?
o: BIS certification is compulsory for domestic and foreign toy makers
Applicable standards include IS 9873 and IS 15644
By May 2026 there were 1,786 foreign and 56 domestic licences
Registered artisans and GI users are exempt
x: The figures are reversed: by May 2026 there were 1,786 domestic and 56 foreign licences.

s: In which year was the first e-Toycathon held?
x: The first e-Toycathon was held in 2025; Toycathon itself dates to 2021.

s: The National Critical Mineral Mission targets how many exploration projects by 2030–31?
x: The Mission targets 1,200 projects; 777 are NMEDT projects, 457 GSI projects and 723 the blocks auctioned since 2015.

s: Which Section of the MMDR Amendment Act 2026 bars States from levying tax or cess on mineral rights except under Centre-prescribed conditions?
x: Section 9D restricts State taxes or cess on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land to Centre-prescribed conditions.

s: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched?
o: Rare earths – Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Kerala
x: Monazite sands are associated with rare-earth occurrence, not lithium.

s: What is the outlay of the critical-mineral recycling scheme introduced in October 2025?
x: The recycling scheme is worth ₹1,500 crore; processing parks are planned in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Odisha and Maharashtra.

s: Which of the following PM MITRA parks is a Brownfield park?
x: Amravati (Maharashtra) is Brownfield; Dhar, Navsari and Kalaburagi are Greenfield.

s: Where is Karnataka's PM MITRA park located?
x: Karnataka's park is at Kalaburagi; Lucknow is in UP, Dhar in MP and Amravati in Maharashtra.

s: Which toy–State pair is correctly matched?
o: Channapatna Toys and Dolls – Tamil Nadu
Channapatna Toys and Dolls – Madhya Pradesh
x: Thanjavur Doll is from Tamil Nadu; Channapatna toys are from Karnataka and Leather Toys from Indore, Madhya Pradesh.

s: What was India's share of global ship recycling in 2025?
x: India's share was 35.4% in 2025; 30.1% was the 2024 figure.

s: Under the Ship Recycling Act, 2019, which body is the National Authority?
o: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
x: The National Authority under the Ship Recycling Act, 2019 is the Directorate General of Shipping, not the Ministry of Textiles.

s: India met its Maritime India Vision 2030 ship-recycling target how many years early?
x: India met the target five years early, in 2025.

s: Alang-Sosiya accounts for approximately what share of India's ship recycling?
x: Alang-Sosiya handles about 98% of India's ship recycling, with about 6 million GT capacity.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the NLCIL–CSIR-CECRI MoU?
o: It concerns extracting rare earths and critical minerals from mine overburden and tailings
CSIR-CECRI was established in 1948 at Karaikal
It supports the National Critical Mineral Mission
NLCIL was set up in 1956 at Neyveli under the Ministry of Coal
x: CSIR-CECRI is at Karaikudi, not Karaikal.

s: Which scheme–outlay pair is correctly matched?
x: PM MITRA's outlay is ₹4,445 crore; BHAVYA is ₹33,660 crore, Modified UDAN ₹28,840 crore and Samudra Manthan ₹84,084 crore.

s: To which countries did India's record seafood exports of 2025–26 mainly go?
x: The top buyers were the USA and China.

s: India and France, with trade of USD 15.81 billion in 2025–26, target trade of how much in five years?
x: The target is USD 32 billion in five years.

s: The PM MITRA scheme is the abbreviation for which of the following?
o: PM Mega Integrated Textile and Apparel Parks
PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel Park
PM Integrated Textile Region and Apparel Parks
PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel Parks
x: PM MITRA stands for PM Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel Parks, implemented by the Ministry of Textiles. The singular form and the versions omitting “Region” are incorrect expansions.

s: In which year was the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana, which supports location-specific State projects, launched?
x: RKVY was launched in 2007, not 2015.

s: Which body assigned separate HSN codes to makhana in 2025?
x: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) assigned separate HSN codes to makhana in 2025.

s: Where is the Marine Products Export Development Authority (MPEDA) headquartered?
x: MPEDA, set up in 1972, has its HQ at Kochi.

s: About how many farmers in India grow cotton?
x: About 6 million farmers grow cotton; 40–50 million people work in cotton processing and trade.

s: In natural farming, what is mulching known as?
x: Mulching is Acchadana; Bijamrutha is seed treatment and Waaphasa is air–moisture balance.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's first soil texture map?
o: It was developed by ICAR–NIHSAD, Bhopal
It is also described as India's first village-level soil-resource map
It is a hectare-level digital map
Soil texture refers to the share of sand, silt and clay in soil
x: The map was developed by ICAR–NBSS&LUP, Nagpur (established 1976), not ICAR–NIHSAD, Bhopal.

s: On which date was the National Mission on Natural Farming approved as a standalone Centrally Sponsored Scheme?
x: The Mission was approved on 25 November 2024.

s: Where was the Southern Regional Conference of World Food India 2026, its first-ever regional edition, held?
x: The Southern Regional Conference was held at Visakhapatnam on 9–10 July 2026.

s: Where is the headquarters of the Coconut Development Board?
x: The Coconut Development Board is headquartered in Kochi.

s: Under the Soil Health Card scheme (2015), how often are cards assessing 12 parameters issued?
x: Soil Health Cards follow a 2-year cycle, assess 12 parameters, and 25.89 crore cards have been generated.

s: In 2006, at what price did Andhra Pradesh cap a Bt cotton seed packet?
x: Andhra Pradesh capped the Bt cotton seed price at ₹750 per packet in 2006.

s: Which policies are associated with States reducing the use of chemical fertilisers?
o: National Mission on Natural Farming and PM-PRANAM
National Mission on Natural Farming and PMKSY
x: The National Mission on Natural Farming and PM-PRANAM are linked to States cutting chemical fertiliser use.

s: To which family does coconut (Cocos nucifera) belong?
x: Coconut is Cocos nucifera of the family Arecaceae.

s: Which scheme provides financial assistance of ₹4,000 per acre per year for two years to promote natural farming?
o: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan
x: The National Mission on Natural Farming provides ₹4,000 per acre per year for two years. The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana is associated with “Per Drop More Crop,” not this assistance.

s: Which Bt cotton technology, with two stacked genes, was introduced in 2006?
x: Bollgard II came in 2006; Bollgard III and RR Flex were never commercialised.

s: Which State's natural farming initiative won the Food Planet Prize 2026?
x: Andhra Pradesh's natural farming initiative won the Food Planet Prize 2026.

s: Which group of States constitutes the southern cotton-growing zone?
x: The southern cotton zone comprises Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan form the northern zone, while Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh form the central zone.

s: What is India's position in global coconut production, accounting for 31.24% of world production?
x: India ranks 1st in global coconut production, with a 31.24% share of world production. The 3rd position refers to India's rank in area under coconut cultivation, not production.

s: Which of the following about State-wise coconut indicators is NOT correct?
o: Kerala has the largest area under coconut
Andhra Pradesh has the highest coconut productivity
West Bengal has the highest coconut productivity
Tamil Nadu has the highest coconut production
x: Andhra Pradesh, not West Bengal, has the highest coconut productivity; West Bengal comes next.

s: In which State was the National Makhana Board launched on 15 September 2025?
x: It was launched in Bihar, after being announced in the Union Budget 2025–26.

s: Besides its other functions, what specialised role does the Coconut Development Board perform for coconut products?
o: It serves as the Export Promotion Council for all agricultural products
It serves as the Export Promotion Council for coconut products except husk and fibre
It procures ball copra for NAFED and NCCF
It operates the National Research Centre for Makhana
x: The Coconut Development Board is the Export Promotion Council for coconut products except husk and fibre. The other options refer to functions or institutions not assigned to the Board in this context.

s: In the coconut sector, what does 'Neera' refer to?
x: Neera is unfermented, zero-alcohol sap; other coconut initiatives include Friends of Coconut Tree, Cocomitra, Kera Kaushal Kendra and Kera Suraksha Insurance.

s: Which of the following is associated with the National Research Centre for Makhana?
o: Development of varieties, makhana-cum-fish farming and popping machines
Assignment of separate HSN codes and export promotion
Procurement of milling copra and ball copra
x: The National Research Centre for Makhana works on varieties, makhana-cum-fish farming and popping machines. HSN-code assignment is associated with DGFT, while the other options concern solar irrigation or copra procurement.

s: Makhana (Euryale ferox) is consumed mainly as its:
x: The edible part of makhana is its seed, called fox nut.

s: Which State accounts for about three-fourths of India's makhana output and 80–85% of global supply?
x: Bihar produces about three-fourths of India's makhana and 80–85% of global supply.

s: How much does one bale of cotton weigh?
x: A bale weighs 170 kg; India is first in cotton area and second in production.

s: By what name is the cotton species Gossypium barbadense known?
x: G. barbadense is Egyptian cotton; India is the only country growing all four cotton species.

s: Which cotton species/staple pair is correctly matched?
x: G. hirsutum is American upland cotton; G. herbaceum is Asian, ELS is 32.5 mm and above, and long staple is 27.5–32 mm.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about cotton procurement in 2025–26?
o: The Cotton Board is the nodal procurement agency
The Cotton Corporation of India had 571 centres
x: The Cotton Corporation of India, not the Cotton Board, is the nodal agency.

s: Cotton cultivation requires about how many frost-free days?
x: Cotton needs about 210 frost-free days and 50–100 cm of rain.

s: Which description best defines natural farming (Prakritik Kheti)?
o: Chemical-free farming based on on-farm biomass and local cattle-based inputs
Chemical farming based on purchased synthetic inputs
Seed treatment based only on lime and soil
Mulching based only on air–moisture balance
x: Natural farming, or Prakritik Kheti, is chemical-free and relies on on-farm biomass and local cattle-based inputs. The option referring only to air–moisture balance describes Waaphasa, not the overall concept of natural farming.

s:
Assertion (A): The Prime Minister appealed for a shift towards natural farming.
Reason (R): The appeal was made amid fertiliser and El Niño risks.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both the appeal for a shift towards natural farming and its context of fertiliser and El Niño risks are correct. The fertiliser and El Niño risks explain why the shift was advocated, making Reason the correct explanation of Assertion.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC)?
o: It was established in 2015 with NABARD
x: NAFCC gives a 100% central grant; 55% is the PMKSY subsidy for small and marginal farmers.

s: Which institution prepared India's first hectare-level soil texture map?
x: The first soil texture map was made by ICAR–NBSS&LUP, Nagpur (est. 1976).

s: India is the only country that grows all four species of which crop?
x: India is the only country growing all four cotton species; 1st in area, 2nd in production.

s: Which State has the highest coconut productivity in India?
x: Kerala has the largest area, Tamil Nadu the highest production, and AP the highest productivity.

s: Approximately what share of rural households in India have broadband access?
x: Broadband access is about 8% among rural households, not 18%.

s: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission primarily focuses on which of the following?
x: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission focuses on indigenous cattle and buffaloes. Pest surveillance and ethanol blending are separate agricultural and biofuel initiatives.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Rashtriya Gokul Mission?
o: It was launched in 2014 by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying
Sex-sorted semen gives female calves with up to 90% accuracy
MAITRIs means Multi-Purpose AI Technicians in Rural India
The Accelerated Breed Improvement Programme gives an incentive of up to 25% of cost on assured pregnancy
x: The incentive under the Accelerated Breed Improvement Programme is up to 50% of the cost on assured pregnancy, not 25%.

s: What was India's record wheat production in 2024–25?
x: Wheat production reached a record 117.94 MT in 2024–25.

s: Which of the following is an agriculture-specific language model?
x: Agri Param is the agriculture-specific language model; Kisan e-Mitra is a voice chatbot and SATHI does QR seed tracing.

s: The study on climate change-related decline in milk yield examined which State of the trans-Gangetic plains?
x: The study examined Haryana, in the trans-Gangetic plains.

s: Which institution produced the world's first IVF female calf of the indigenous Lakhimi breed?
o: ICAR–Central Institute for Research on Buffaloes, Hisar
x: The world's first IVF Lakhimi female calf was achieved by Assam Veterinary and Fishery University.

s: In the IVF process behind the world's first Lakhimi female calf, which step comes right after egg collection?
x: The sequence is egg collection, maturation, fertilisation, embryo development and embryo transfer.

s: In Haryana, during which months is heat stress on milk production worst?
x: The worst conditions occur in July–August, when temperature exceeds 38°C and humidity exceeds 70%.

s: What was India's milk production in 2024–25?
x: Milk production rose from 146.3 MMT in 2014–15 to 247.87 MMT in 2024–25, a growth of 69.41%.

s: Which exotic cattle breed pair is correctly matched?
o: Guernsey – Golden milk associated with beta-carotene
Red Dane – Golden milk associated with beta-carotene
x: Guernsey is known for golden milk (beta-carotene); Red Dane is from Denmark and Ayrshire from Scotland.

s: What CAGR did India's livestock sector record?
x: The livestock sector recorded a CAGR of 12.77%.

s: What is India's position in global meat production?
x: India is fourth globally in meat, second in eggs and the largest producer of milk.

s: Namo Drone Didi is correctly described as which of the following?
o: A Central Sector Scheme for women SHGs under DAY-NRLM
A Centrally Sponsored Scheme for women SHGs under DAY-NRLM
A Central Sector Scheme for farmer producer organisations under DAY-NRLM
A State Sector Scheme for women SHGs under DAY-NRLM
x: Namo Drone Didi is a Central Sector Scheme meant for women SHGs under DAY-NRLM. The most tempting wrong option calls it a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, whereas its classification is Central Sector.

s: Which cattle breed–origin pair is correctly matched?
x: Sahiwal is linked to Montgomery; Red Sindhi to Karachi/Hyderabad and Jersey to Jersey Island, UK.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the registered breeds covered under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission?
x: Gir, Ongole and Red Sindhi are covered indigenous breeds; Jersey is not in the list.

s: What is Bharat-VISTAAR?
o: An AI-enabled multilingual farm advisory platform
x: Bharat-VISTAAR is an AI-enabled multilingual farm advisory platform; the agriculture-specific language model is Agri Param.

s: What was India's per capita milk availability in 2024–25?
x: Milk 247.87 MMT in 2024-25; per capita 485 g/day.

s: Tourism contributes about what share of India's GDP?
x: Tourism contributes about 7% of GDP and over 9% of employment.

s: WTTC projects India's travel and tourism contribution at USD 523 billion by 2034, making it the world's ____-largest tourism economy.
x: WTTC ranks India as the 4th-largest tourism economy, not the 5th.

s: The National Logistics Policy targets which World Bank Logistics Performance Index rank for India by 2030?
x: The policy targets a top-25 LPI rank by 2030; India was 38th in 2023. PM Gati Shakti is a GIS platform with 58 ministries.

s: Vision@2047 targets how many international visitors to India by 2047?
x: Vision@2047 targets 100 million international visitors by 2047.

s: For what speed is the 508-km Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail designed?
x: The Mumbai–Ahmedabad HSR is 508 km long and designed for 320 kmph; Kavach had been deployed on 3,103 route km.

s: Maritime transport handles about what share of India's trade by volume and by value, respectively?
x: Maritime transport handles 95% of India's trade by volume and 70% by value; National Waterways rose from 5 to 111.

s: Which is the world's first equatorial Satellite-Based Augmentation System (SBAS)?
x: India's GAGAN is the world's first equatorial SBAS.

s: What is the e-Samudra portal launched under maritime digitalisation?
o: A single-window, faceless digital maritime portal for seafarers, shipping firms, training institutes and ports
A 24x7 grievance-redressal portal exclusively for seafarers
A cargo-tracking portal for major ports only
A recruitment portal for the Indian Navy
x: e-Samudra is a single-window, faceless maritime portal; the 24x7 seafarer grievance portal is e-Navik.

s: Which is India's first cable-stayed railway bridge?
x: Anji Khad is India's first cable-stayed railway bridge; Pamban is the first vertical-lift railway sea bridge.

s: Which is the world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 ft?
x: Atal Tunnel is the world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 ft.

s: Which two places does the East-West Corridor connect?
x: The East-West Corridor runs Silchar–Porbandar; Moreh–Mae Sot is the Trilateral Highway.

s: Which is India's first river interlinking project?
x: Ken–Betwa is India's first river interlinking project.

s: FAITH has demanded that how many tourism destinations be developed in mission mode?
x: FAITH demands 50 destinations in mission mode, along with uniform industry status in all States.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the first double-stack long-haul container train from JNPA?
o: It covered about 422 km carrying 360 TEUs
It ran to CONCOR's Gateway Container Terminal at Varnama
x: Varnama is in Gujarat, not Maharashtra.

s: In which year was the Container Corporation of India (CONCOR) established?
x: CONCOR was established in 1988.

s: In the context of India's tourism and hospitality sector, what does FAITH stand for?
o: Federation of Agencies in Indian Tourism and Hospitality
Federation of Associations in Indian Tourism and Hospitality
Federation of Associations in Indian Finance and Hospitality
Forum of Associations in Indian Tourism and Hotels
x: FAITH stands for Federation of Associations in Indian Tourism and Hospitality and is the apex body in the sector. The other expansions do not represent the organisation identified in the tourism context.

s: The Digital India Bhashini–GeM MoU provides for procurement in how many official languages?
x: The MoU covers all 22 official languages.

s: The Blue Valley Cluster Programme is a collaboration between Assam and which organisation?
x: The Blue Valley Cluster Programme is a collaboration between Assam and the European Union, focusing on bioeconomy industries such as natural fragrances, spices and AYUSH. The Asian Development Bank and the Ministry of AYUSH are associated with other facts, not this collaboration.

s: To which State does the Bairabi–Sairang railway line provide a rail link?
x: Bairabi–Sairang links Mizoram by rail.

s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Anji Khad – World's highest railway arch bridge
Chenab Bridge – First cable-stayed railway bridge
Pamban – First vertical-lift railway sea bridge
x: Pamban is the first vertical-lift sea bridge; Chenab the highest arch bridge; Anji Khad the first cable-stayed; Bairabi–Sairang links Mizoram.

s: What was India's rank in the World Bank Logistics Performance Index 2023?
x: India's LPI rank improved from 54 (2014) to 38 (2023); target top 25 by 2030.

s: How many National Waterways does India have now?
x: National Waterways rose from 5 to 111.
